Asymmetric Catalysis
Iridium-Catalyzed Enantioselective Formal meta-Allenylation of
Pyridines
Pankaj Roy+, Pratibha Mahto+, and Santanu Mukherjee*
Abstract: Site-selective functionalization of pyridines is an important yet challenging transformation. Temporary
dearomatization of pyridines through redox-neutral cycloaddition has recently emerged as a reliable and attractive strategy
for meta-functionalization of pyridines. Despite the amenability of the resulting bench-stable cycloadduct, oxazinopyridine,
to a variety of electrophilic and radical-based reagents, its enantioselective functionalization remains unexplored. Herein,
we present the first enantioselective meta-functionalization of pyridines through the intermediacy of oxazinopyridines. This
highly enantioselective formal meta-allenylation of pyridines is achieved by treating the easily accessible oxazinopyridines
with racemic allenylic alcohol under the combination of a catalytic amount of an Ir(I)/(P, olefin) complex and Lewis
acidic Sc(OTf) followed by acid-mediated rearomatization. With oxazinopyridines derived from unsubstituted or suitably
substituted pyridines, iterative 3,5-difunctionalization is possible, which also allows for the stereodivergent synthesis of all
four stereoisomers of 3,5-bis-allenylic pyridines.
Introduction
Pyridine is among the most abundant nitrogenous het-
erocycles in natural products,<sup>[1]</sup> pharmaceuticals,<sup>[2–4]</sup> and
agrochemicals<sup>[5]</sup> (Figure 1). Pyridine derivatives also serve
as ligands<sup>[6]</sup> and catalysts<sup>[7,8]</sup> in asymmetric synthesis besides
acting as precursors to targets of biological and material
importance.<sup>[9]</sup> Consequently, site-selective functionalization
of pyridines is a highly sought-after transformation. Direct
C–H functionalization is the most straightforward avenue
of decorating pyridines.<sup>[10,11]</sup> The inherent electron-deficient
nature of pyridines renders their ortho- and para-positions
electrophilic and amenable to nucleophilic substitution
(Scheme 1a).<sup>[12,13]</sup> In contrast, meta-functionalization of
pyridines is challenging.<sup>[14–16]</sup> Electrophilic aromatic substi-
tution reactions such as nitration<sup>[17]</sup> and bromination<sup>[18]</sup> of
pyridines are known but require harsh reaction conditions,
which restrict their application.
The adversities associated with functionalizing the meta-
position of pyridines have spurred innovative strategies
in recent years.<sup>[14,15]</sup> Various approaches, including
directing group-assisted C–H activation,<sup>[19,20]</sup> non-directed
metalation,<sup>[21–23]</sup> and temporary dearomatization of the
pyridine ring,<sup>[24,25]</sup> have been explored to enable meta-
functionalization, of which the latter emerged as the most
attractive one (Scheme 1b). Among different temporary
dearomatization strategies adopted so far,<sup>[24,26–31]</sup> the redox-
neutral dearomatization of pyridine through cycloaddition is
particularly noteworthy.
In 1967, Huisgen et al. reported a three-component
cycloaddition of pyridine or isoquinoline with dimethyl
acetylenedicarboxylate (DMAD) and phenyl isocyanate,
which could be converted back to its components upon
heating.<sup>[32]</sup> The Nair group further advanced this area by
substituting phenyl isocyanate with other dipolarophiles,
thereby expanding the scope of this reaction.<sup>[33–36]</sup>
Notwithstanding the reversibility of this cycloaddition
reaction, its potential in functionalizing pyridines was not
realized until recently. In 2022, Studer et al. exploited
this strategy to transform pyridines into bench-stable
dearomatized oxazinopyridines C, via Huisgen 1,4-
dipolar cycloaddition with DMAD and methyl pyruvate
(Scheme 1b).<sup>[28]</sup> These oxazinopyridines (oxazinoazines)
are nucleophilic in nature by virtue of their (di)enamine
character and may be viewed as meta-nucleophilic pyridine
surrogates. Consequently, they have been intercepted with a
variety of electrophiles and radical-based reagents prior to
rearomatization to afford meta-substituted pyridines.<sup>[28,37–41]</sup>
In addition, meta-sulfonylation of pyridines has also been
achieved under electrochemical<sup>[42]</sup> or photochemical
conditions.<sup>[43,44]</sup>
Despite their growing popularity, the application of these
meta-nucleophilic pyridine surrogates in catalytic transforma-
tions is rare.<sup>[40,43]</sup> Moreover, this redox-neutral dearomati-
zation strategy has never been applied for enantioselective
functionalization of pyridines or any other azines. In fact,
the only examples of enantioselective meta-functionalization
of pyridines, reported by Wang et al., involve reductive
dearomatization of pyridines.<sup>[45,46]</sup> These processes comprise
of borane-catalyzed dearomative hydroboration of pyridines
to 1,4-dihydropyridines (A, Scheme 1b) followed by Pd-
or Ir-catalyzed enantioselective meta-allylation and oxidative
rearomatization.

In an effort to expand the synthetic toolbox for enan-
tioselective functionalization of pyridines with precise meta-
regioselectivity, we herein report the first enantioselective
functionalization of oxazinopyridines en route to chiral meta-
functionalized pyridines.<sup>[47]</sup>
As a part of our research program on enantioselec-
tive C(sp<sup>2</sup>)–H allenylation under iridium catalysis,<sup>[48,49]</sup> we
became interested in introducing an allenylic substituent at
the meta-position of pyridines. Ir-catalyzed allenylic sub-
stitution reaction was first reported by Takeuchi et al.
in 2004.<sup>[50]</sup> However, Ir-catalyzed enantioselective allenylic
substitution was pioneered by the Carreira group and was
proposed to proceed via an Ir-bound allenylic carbocation
intermediate.<sup>[51–53]</sup> Recent studies by our laboratory<sup>[48]</sup> and
the Takeuchi group<sup>[54]</sup> demonstrated the utility of this catalyst
system for Friedel–Crafts allenylation of (hetero)arenes.
However, electron-deficient nature of pyridines precludes
their direct application in Friedel–Crafts allenylation.

tionality of oxazinopyridines<sup>[28]</sup> can be intercepted with an
Ir-bound electrophilic allenylic fragment<sup>[53]</sup> (Scheme 1c).

chiral pyridine derivatives, bearing a synthetically versatile
allenylic group at the meta-position.

Similarly, 3-substituted pyridines can give rise to two
regioisomeric oxazinopyridines, which are inseparable. How-
ever, each of these oxazinopyridines contains only one
accessible position for allenylation and upon rearomatization
should converge into the same product. As expected from the
reaction with 2a, catalyst controlled-enantioinduction should
override the substrate control. Indeed, when oxazinopyridine
2b, derived from 3-methyl pyridine 1b, was reacted as a
mixture of diastereo- and regioisomers in a 1:1.2 ratio with
rac-3a, the 3-allenylic 5-methyl pyridine 5ba was isolated
in 68% yield with >99.5:0.5 e.r. (Scheme 2b). Clearly, each
isomer of 2b yields the same product enantiomer upon
rearomatization with equally high enantioselectivity.
Having optimized the reaction conditions, the scope and
limitations of meta-allenylation of pyridines were investi-
gated. We first sought to examine the scope of pyridines
in this reaction (Scheme 3). A variety of oxazinopyridines
(2b-q), derived from 3-substituted pyridines, reacted effi-
ciently with allenylic alcohol rac-3a under our optimized
reaction conditions. In all these cases, the isomeric mixtures
of oxazinopyridines were employed as substrate, and the
corresponding meta-allenylic pyridines 5ba-qa were obtained
in moderate to good yields over two steps with uniformly
outstanding e.r. Electron-rich oxazinopyridines (2b-h) turned
out to be superior substrates compared to most of the
electron-deficient ones (2i-q), as the products with relatively
higher yields were generally observed with the former.
Protected functionalities on oxazinopyridines such as NHBoc
(2e), OAc (2g), acetal (2l) didn’t hamper the allenylation
reaction, but the protecting groups fell off under the acidic
conditions employed for the rearomatization step. However,
we were pleased to note that other functional groups such as
amide and ketone survived all three steps.

In the case of 2-substituted pyridines, availability of both
3- and 5-positions gives rise to the possibility of regioiso-
meric allenylation apart from bis-allenylation. Interestingly,
oxazinopyridine 2r, derived from 2-phenyl pyridine, did
not pose any regioselectivity issue and furnished 2-phenyl
5-allenylic pyridine 5ra exclusively with excellent enantios-
electivity, albeit in only 32% yield. The same trend was
observed with other 2-aryl pyridine-derived oxazinopyridines
(2s-u). In these instances, allenylation proceeded through
the dienamine functionality of the oxazinopyridine to avoid
steric repulsion with the aryl substituent. To the best of our
knowledge, this is the first example of enantioselective C5-
functionalization of 2-aryl pyridines. Unfortunately, 2-alkyl
pyridines failed to react in the Huisgen 1,4-dipolar cycloaddi-
tion step to generate oxazinopyridines and, therefore, aren’t
compatible with this dearomative meta-allenylation strategy.
2-Heteroaryl pyridines furnished the desired product but in
low yield (see Supporting Information).
4-Methyl pyridine-derived oxazinopyridine 2v is also
amenable to allenylation under our optimized reaction con-
ditions and led only to mono-allenylation: The 3-allenylic
4-methyl pyridine 5va was isolated in moderate yield with
high enantiopurity. 5,6,7,8-Tetrahydroisoquinoline (1w) via
dearomative meta-allenylation gave access to polysubstituted
pyridine 5wa in decent yield.
Subsequently, we became interested in exploring other
structurally related azines, such as quinoline, isoquinoline,
etc., under our protocol. While the dearomatized interme-
diate derived from quinoline did not participate in the
allenylation reaction, isoquinoline (1x) smoothly produced
4-allenylic isoquinoline 5xa in 37% yield with 95.5:4.5 e.r.

explore the scope of allenylic alcohols (Scheme 4). For this
purpose, oxazinopyridine 2b, derived from 3-methyl pyridine
(1b), was selected as the nucleophile. An array of electron-
rich (3b-d) and electron-deficient (3e-g) para-substituted aryl
allenylic alcohols underwent successful substitution reaction
with 3-methyl oxazinopyridine (2b) and delivered the 3-
allenylic 5-methyl pyridines (5bb-bg) in moderate to good

stereocenters and are used as a mixture of diastereomers in
racemic form. While an inherent substrate bias over stereoin-
duction in the allenylation step gives rise to the likelihood of a
match/mismatch scenario, powerful catalyst control rules out
such a possibility, and meta-allenylic pyridines are obtained
with high e.r. in each case.
